analysis_trace: Trial NCT06256432 is a Phase 2, multi-center, randomized, open-label study comparing low-dose ambrisentan (two experimental arms) versus terlipressin (active comparator) in patients with hepatorenal syndrome (HRS). Primary endpoint is change in eGFR at 4 days; secondary endpoints include HRS reversal at 14 days, HRS recurrence at 60 days, and overall survival at 60 days.

Evidence retrieved: (1) CONFIRM trial data showing terlipressin achieves ~32% verified HRS reversal vs 17% placebo; (2) Endothelin receptor antagonist review (PMC11869344) demonstrating ET-1 role in renal vasoconstriction and ERA potential to improve GFR; (3) Ambrisentan preclinical data (PMC5533228) showing preservation of GFR and reduction in proteinuria in sickle cell nephropathy model.

Evidence-role assessment: CONFIRM trial provides direct_numeric for terlipressin response rates; ERA mechanism papers provide indirect_direction for ambrisentan efficacy; no direct ambrisentan HRS trial data available. Mismatch: ambrisentan studies are in different populations (CKD, sickle cell) not HRS.

Primary endpoint (eGFR change at 4 days): No direct ambrisentan HRS data. Based on ERA mechanism improving renal perfusion and terlipressin comparator data showing renal function improvement, predict modest eGFR increase with ambrisentan. Confidence low due to lack of HRS-specific ambrisentan data.

Secondary-0 (HRS reversal at 14 days): Terlipressin historical rate ~32-39%. Ambrisentan mechanism plausible but unproven in HRS. Predict lower reversal rate for ambrisentan vs terlipressin given lack of vasoconstrictor mechanism. Confidence low.

Secondary-1 (HRS recurrence at 60 days): Limited data on recurrence rates. Terlipressin recurrence after reversal ~30-40%. Ambrisentan unknown. Predict similar or higher recurrence with ambrisentan due to less robust initial response.

Secondary-2 (Overall survival at 60 days): HRS mortality high without treatment. Terlipressin improves survival vs placebo. Ambrisentan survival benefit unproven. Predict survival proportion ~50-60% across arms given severity of underlying disease.

Safety considerations: Ambrisentan at low doses (<250 mcg/day) may have less fluid retention risk than standard PAH doses. Hepatotoxicity risk requires monitoring. Terlipressin known risks include ischemic events.
Key uncertainty: No published ambrisentan HRS clinical trial results; all predictions based on mechanism and indirect evidence from other populations.

Trial outcome prediction: Uncertain - Phase 2 exploratory design with novel mechanism; ambrisentan may show signals of renal benefit but unlikely to demonstrate superiority to terlipressin for HRS reversal.
